title: 2011 AMC 12A Problem 18
statement: Suppose that \(|x + y| + |x - y| = 2.\) What is the maximum possible value of \(x^2 - 6x + y^2?\)

solutions.text:
The identity \(|x+y| + |x-y|\) \(= 2\max(|x|, |y|)\) turns the condition into \(\max(|x|, |y|) = 1,\) the boundary of the square with \(|x| \le 1\) and \(|y| \le 1.\)

On this region \(x^2 - 6x + y^2\) increases as \(x\) decreases and as \(y^2\) increases, so the maximum is at \(x = -1,\) \(y = \pm 1:\) \[ 1 + 6 + 1 = 8. \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The equation \(|x+y| + |x-y| = 2\) means \(\max(|x|, |y|) = 1,\) the boundary of the square \([-1,1]^2\)
On that square, \(x^2 - 6x + y^2\) is largest when \(x = -1\) and \(y = \pm 1\)
